title: Observability shim: async event-forwarder + metric compactification to cut tail latency and cardinality
creator: Ava Chen
description: Reduce end-to-end tail latency and metric cardinality by introducing an async observability shim that decouples sync log/tracing hooks from request-critical paths, consolidate meter exporters, and apply a lightweight OpenTelemetry dependency upgrade. This ticket covers: 1) a small C++/Go shim that accepts in-process events over a fast socket and forwards to the exporter asynchronously, 2) migration from multiple meter exporters to a single batched exporter with backpressure, 3) normalization of high-cardinality labels (user_id, request_id) using controlled hashing and label whitelists, 4) replace blocking flush calls in runtime with non-blocking flush-with-timeout behavior, 5) update CI benchmarks and add perf regression tests.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P95 token-latency impact from observability hooks <= +2ms on steady-state synthetic load
P99 tail reduction >= 20% vs baseline (measurement harness link in artifacts)
Metric cardinality for request-related meters reduced by >= 70% (measured after whitelist rules applied)
All services compile and pass unit/integration tests with OpenTelemetry upgraded to v1.27.0 and our shim integrated
No increase in dropped spans > 0.5% under sustained 10k rps synthetic load; dropped events are recorded to diagnostics exporter
tasks: Design async shim API and socket protocol (small binary, keep dependencies minimal)
Prototype shim in Go using unix domain sockets & efficient batch buffering
Add exporter that reads shim batches and writes to existing OTLP collector with batching/backoff
Implement label normalization rules and config-driven whitelist in runtime
Replace blocking flush() calls with flush-with-timeout and non-blocking drain paths
Update OpenTelemetry SDK dependency in runtime and reconcile any breaking API changes
Add canary rollout plan and runtime flag to toggle shim per-service
Create perf harness with realistic prompt lengths and KV-cache warm/cold scenarios
Benchmark P95/P99 and iterate on buffer sizing and retry/backoff parameters
Document configuration knobs and add runbook for troubleshooting dropped events
